description: We are Volodymyr Chyzhevskyi and Andrii Khomych, a Ukrainian team from Zhytomyr Polytechnic passionate about technology, engineering, and innovation. We won 1st place at HackTheFICT and RE: ACCESS ZHYTOMYR, and 2nd place at STEM Hackathon. Our individual achievements include national and international awards in programming, software development, research, and engineering. We combine complementary skills, creativity, and a strong drive to build impactful solutions.
summary: LUNAVEX is a web platform for exploring potential landing sites near the Moon’s south pole. It combines an interactive map using NASA Moon Trek services and LRO imagery with LOLA-derived elevation readings. Users can select, save, and compare site information, then run separate, time-based analyses of the apparent positions of the Sun and Earth using JPL Horizons data. The Sun & Illumination Analyzer displays solar azimuth and elevation, while EarthLink identifies periods when Earth’s center is above the geometric horizon. Research can be saved and exported as CSV or JSON. LUNAVEX helps mission planners, educators, and the public explore lunar site conditions in one place. These analyses are preliminary: they do not model local terrain shadows, actual solar power output, or complete radio-link performance.
details:
LUNAVEX is a web platform for exploring candidate landing sites near the Moon’s south pole. In the Lunar Site Explorer, users can view LRO LROC WAC imagery, switch to LOLA elevation data, select locations, and save or compare site information such as coordinates, observation time, available elevation readings, and data sources. The LOLA reading is relative to the Moon’s mean radius; it is not a detailed model of the surrounding terrain.

Users can open a saved site in the Sun & Illumination Analyzer or EarthLink, choose a date range and time step, and request ephemeris data from JPL Horizons. The Sun analyzer displays solar azimuth and elevation over time. EarthLink displays Earth’s apparent position and identifies periods when Earth’s center is above the geometric horizon. Studies can be saved and exported as CSV or JSON. Analyses for different sites or dates are run separately; the platform does not automatically overlay multiple ephemeris studies for side-by-side comparison.

LUNAVEX also includes LunaEnergy, LunaRadiation, LunaThermo, and Artemis II Lab for exploring additional educational scenarios. These calculators use simplified models and are not certified engineering tools. The project is designed for mission planners, educators, and the public. It aims to make lunar site research easier to explore and document. Future development could add side-by-side comparisons of saved Sun and Earth studies, terrain-aware shadow analysis, and more detailed power and communication models.

The interface is built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The server uses Node.js and Express, and PostgreSQL stores accounts and saved research. NASA resources include Moon Trek, LRO LROC WAC imagery, and LOLA elevation data. JPL Horizons provides ephemeris data.
